furniture/furn_solenne_wardrobe_a.json: A lacquered cabinet in dark walnut, brass-cornered, its doors easing open at your approach and never quite slamming. Inside: a lit rail, cedar air held a degree cooler than the room, a brass plate reading VALET BY POLARIS. It'll lay out a look, and it has opinions about the ones you don't ask for.
furniture/furn_cherry_hookah.json: A tall brass hookah stood in the middle of the low table, four hoses coiled like something asleep. The glass is cloudy with everything that has been through it, and the bowl is scrubbed exactly as often as it needs, which is less often than you'd like. The mouthpieces are wiped between guests.
furniture/furniture_asc_vat_ledger.json: A lectern of dark wood, absurd in a room like this, holding a book that is updated by hand. Names, dates, withdrawals, in a careful clerical script with no corrections, running back further than the building has. Nowhere is there a figure in credits. That conversation happens at Halcyon.
furniture/furn_jolenes_piano.json: An upright with the front panel off, so the hammers and felt and the whole embarrassing mechanism are on display. Somebody put drawing pins in the hammer felts forty years ago, which is why it sounds like a bar rather than a parlour. A jam jar on top holds coins and a card: REQUESTS ARE NOT A RIGHT.
furniture/furn_ration9_kitchenware.json: A single bay at the end of the aisle given over to the things you cook IN rather than the things you cook. Pans hang off a length of reinforcing bar, pots nest on the bottom shelf, and the spoons and tongs bristle out of a catering tin nobody has ever emptied. Everything's priced to outlive you.
furniture/furn_bld_897_1175_contraband_t: Cargo stacked shoulder-high under oil-stained tarps: crates, drums, long flat cases the shape of things you don't say out loud. The stencils are painted over, burned off, or in a hand nobody will read to you. It came in on a plane and it'll leave on one. In between, it's nobody's.
furniture/furn_solenne_tv_penthouse.json: A wall-spanning micro-LED panel in a frameless machined-titanium mount, edge-to-edge black glass that vanishes into the room when it's dark and detonates into colour when it's not. The kind of set that costs more than the apartments below it, installed for a man who watches himself on it.
furniture/furn_solenne_salon_espresso.js: A lever machine in unlacquered brass and walnut, two groups, the eagle on top rubbed dull where sixty years of hands have steadied themselves on it. It predates the building. Nothing about it's automatic; the pressure comes off a spring and a forearm. A brass tube at the side warms the cups.
furniture/furn_mintcond_tapewall.json: Floor to ceiling pigeonholes, one tape to a hole, alphabetised and numbered. In front of each is a card slot holding either a blank card, meaning the tape is in, or a name and a date in blunt pencil, meaning it's out and when it's due. Two of them have names with a line drawn under them, twice.
furniture/furn_solenne_fridge_d.json: Brushed alloy, a shelf array that reconfigures itself around whatever you put in it, and an interior glow that comes on a half-second before the door's open, like it's been expecting you. A drop-freezer box sits up top. The brass plate reads POLARIS EXECUTIVE, in a font too tasteful to be honest.
furniture/furn_junkyard_crane.json: A pedestal crane in a yellow chosen once, decades ago, and touched up ever since with whatever yellow was going. The grab hangs open at the end of its cable, five hydraulic fingers spread, close enough to the ground to stand in. People do. There's a wedding photograph taped inside the shack window.
furniture/furn_echelon_bridge_helm.json: The helm: a single slab of dark glass canted toward the forward window, the Basin thrown across it in cold navigational vectors. One worn brass throttle stands proud of it, the only analogue thing aboard. A slow blue pulse breathes under the surface, holding station, waiting for a course.
furniture/furn_cardmint_citadel.json: A brass-cased press set into the marble beside the cash terminals, small enough to miss and loud enough not to. The card slot is taped over and the camera lens behind it has been unscrewed and taken away. Where STRIKE YOUR OWN used to be: CIVIC SELF-ISSUANCE HAS BEEN DISCONTINUED.
furniture/furn_zone_solenne_penthouse_ba: A soaking tub hewn from one block of the same grey stone as the walls, deep enough to disappear in. It fills from a slot in the rim with no visible tap, the water sheeting in silent and steaming. It faces the whole bay: a bath with a hundred-mile view and nothing able to look back.
furniture/furn_echelon_helipad_fuel.json: A squat refuelling bowser lashed to the deck at the pad's edge: a scuffed avgas tank on a wheeled cradle, a coiled grounding cable, a dead-man nozzle in a spring clip. A brass placard reads AVGAS 100LL · GROUND BEFORE FUELLING. Fill a container here, or refuel an aircraft parked on the pad.
furniture/furn_backroom_poker_table.json: A modest oval of green felt, hand-worn, ringed by four club chairs under one low lamp. No chip readers, no screens: a hand-shuffled deck squared at the dealer's end and a brass tray of chips going dull. Cards are dealt by hand and called aloud, so you can play it blind and keep the thread.
furniture/furn_reach_jobboard.json: A stretch of bare planking beside the bar, shingled in index cards, torn envelope backs and one whole ration label, each held on by whatever was to hand: a nail, a knife, one spent round hammered flat. Nothing on it's signed and nothing says who's paying. Read the wall, or type gigs.
furniture/furn_sump_slag_crate.json: A splintered dock crate shoved against the wall, stencilled SUMP HOUSE STOCK: DO NOT WALK OFF WITH. Inside, foam-wrapped slag orbs gone grey with handling, each dense enough to sit you down and soft enough that you get back up. Taped to the lid: FIRST ROUND OF THE NIGHT IS FREE.
furniture/furniture_asc_vat_colonnade.js: Close up, the gold is fine pipework laid over the glass the way a jeweller would lay it, and every tank is warm to the palm. Inside, a body hangs in amber at the temperature of blood, unfinished in ways you do not look at twice. An enamel plate carries a name, a policy number, and a date.
furniture/furn_bed_zone_meridian_unit_10: A mass-produced sleeping slab: thin foam sagging on a dented aluminium frame, stamped with a faded ARCOLOGY HOUSING lot number. The foam took the shape of everyone who slept here before you, and none of them slept well. Cheap, but after a day in the sprawl it might as well be a cloud.
furniture/furn_thorn_tally.json:
Four hundred and eleven marks in chalk, in rows, going back thirty years, in four different symbols.

There's a key at the bottom in small letters. Three hundred and sixty. Thirty-eight. Nine. Four.

Nobody has rubbed out the last group, and the wall beside the board is clean and empty.
furniture/furn_cardmint_gallery.json: A mint press bolted between two rows of deposit boxes, on the theory that anyone already storing valuables might like to become one. It's dark. The queue rail has been folded flat against the wall, and the notice cable-tied to it sends you to a shop on Ironside with an approximate map on the back.
furniture/furn_voltage_djbooth.json: A DJ booth raised on a black plinth like an altar, banked with decks and a wall of faders under a low blue glow. Behind it a figure in a mirrored visor rides the room: hands never still, head down, feeling the crowd through the soles of their feet. The music is the conversation.
furniture/furn_bt_smokehouse.json: A black steel cabinet the height of a person, its door seal furred with three decades of tar, its racks stepped up the inside. It runs at a temperature the manual would call low and slow, and the manual is long gone. What comes out is why the regulars cross the district.
furniture/furn_exo_stillwell.json:
A basin four feet across, cut from one stone and sunk flush into the floor, filled to the brim and not a hair over. The surface is completely flat.

While you're looking, a ring goes out from the middle, reaches the stone and comes back. Nothing dropped. Nothing moved. The air hasn't stirred.
furniture/furn_junkyard_ledger.json: A hardback book the size of a paving slab, open near the back. Left column: what came in. Middle: what was paid. Right, narrower and in a different pen: where it came from, when the answer was interesting. That column is the actual business, and everybody who reads this far works it out at once.
furniture/furn_thorn_maskrack.json:
Eleven masks. Bone, plate, horn, a jaw wired open, one with too many sockets and nothing behind them.

Every one is lined. Quilted rag, stitched flat at every edge so it doesn't chafe on a long shift, and two were re-lined this season. A needle is still stuck in the cloth of the second one.
furniture/furn_mintcond_window.json: The back of the display window, seen from inside: nine comics on nine easels under nine little lamps, each sleeved inside a rigid holder and turned to catch the light off the street. Every one faces out. From in here you get nine blank backing boards, which the proprietor considers no flaw at all.
furniture/furn_mintcond_counter.json: A long glass case lit from beneath, so everything in it sits on a shelf of white light: cards in hard sleeves, laid out in rows with the corners squared to each other. A soft cloth is folded on top of the glass and it isn't decorative. Under the till, a paperback with the spine broken flat.
furniture/furn_cell_showers.json: Six heads on one length of galvanised pipe, no stalls, no curtain, no taps you control. A timer somewhere else in the building decides when the water comes and how long it stays, and it comes lukewarm at best and grey-smelling always. Two heads are capped off with plumber's tape and a shrug.
furniture/furn_neonvig_slots_3.json: The oldest machine on the floor, mahogany-cased and hand-lettered THE WIDOW MAKER in flaking gold leaf. It smells of ozone and old cigarettes, and the lever takes both hands and a grudge. The story goes it once paid a jackpot so large the house was rebuilt around the debt. Feed it credits and pull.
furniture/furn_ration9_counter.json: A scarred laminate counter with a register bolted to it, a rack of gum along the front edge, and a scanner window worn cloudy by four decades of groceries dragged over it. A card taped beside the till reads ALL ITEMS MUST BE PRESENTED. Dell Fry stands behind it, having heard every excuse.
furniture/furn_jolenes_stage.json: Two feet of decking on beer crates, carpeted in something that was red. A stool, a microphone on a boom bent permanently to one height, and a strip of tape marking where to stand so the fan doesn't catch the wig. The boom is set low. Whoever set it wasn't tall and wasn't adjusting it for anybody.
furniture/furn_the_reach_870_1958_fuel_b: A battered fuel bowser on flat, cracked tyres, parked where the packed-dust runway meets the apron. The tank is streaked with spilled avgas and desert varnish, the delivery hose looped over a hook worn bright. It hasn't moved under its own power in years. Everything that needs fuel comes to it.
A double row of avgas drums chocked against the wall, hand-pump clamped to the nearest and a length of hose coiled over it. Chalk tallies climb the drums: fuel run out to strangers, paid or owed. Out here the sky is the only road, and this is the toll booth. Wired to the pump: CASH ON THE SKID.
furniture/furn_thorn_rail.json:
From up here the Thornwarren is laid out below you, the wall goes round all of it, and the red country goes on past the wall.

On the underside of the rail, where you'd only see it lying down, somebody has written small: WE BUILT THIS. It's a note to whoever is up here next.
furniture/furn_voltage_dancefloor.json: A dancefloor sunk two steps into the middle of the room, its surface a lattice of blue-white cells lit from underneath, pulsing in time with the music. Step down and the whole grid answers your weight with light. There's one correct thing to do here, and the room forgives you for being bad at it.
furniture/furn_bt_case.json: A glass-fronted case the width of the shop, trays ranked on crushed ice topped up twice a day and grey by closing. The light inside is deliberately warm, which does the meat a favour it hasn't earned. Prices are inked on card flags stuck into the trays, several crossed out more than once.
furniture/furn_twocell_practice_rig.json: A dead hololock panel on a scaffold board, wired to a scoreboard cannibalised from a dartboard. A card taped beneath it reads: BREAK IT ALL YOU LIKE. NOTHING BEHIND IT BUT THE WALL. The lock cycles a fresh sequence every time it's beaten, and buzzes like a wasp in a tin when it isn't.
furniture/furn_exo_drawing.json:
A very tall structure, in section, dimensioned to the sixteenth of an inch, drawn in three hands over what must be twenty years. The middle third is in a small neat hand. The top is older and looser. The corrections are heavy and recent and there are many.

No title, no date, no name.
furniture/furn_reach_cache_bonepile.json: Someone dug a pit under the trailer bed and covered it back over, and someone has been opening it ever since: the fill is loose, and the tarp edge shows at one corner where the last hand was in a hurry. A pallet comes up out of there sand-drifted and heavy as a body. Not a thing you carry.
furniture/furn_thorn_rack.json:
Eleven blades and no two alike. A hooked pommel for a hand with no thumb. A two-hand haft with the grips a hand apart in height. One with no handle at all, only a hide-lined socket, because it went onto something grown to a point.

Every one was made for somebody. Some of them are still alive.
furniture/furn_the_reach_870_1958_windso: A sun-bleached windsock on a leaning steel pole, faded from orange to the colour of old bone and patched with tape at the throat. It's the closest thing Buzzard Field has to a control tower: read it right and it tells you which way to come in, read it wrong and the scrub tells you the rest.
furniture/furn_ration9_microwave.json: A scuffed beige box bolted to the end of the counter, its cracked turntable grinding round a half-second behind the motor. The interior light died some time ago, so whatever's in there goes around in the dark. Somebody has scratched out the numbers and written HOT and VERY HOT above two buttons.
furniture/furn_secdesk_zone_meridian_lob: A curved reception desk in scuffed laminate, built to be manned around the clock. The chair behind it's long gone. A dead terminal cycles rolling static, throwing a faint grey flicker across the underside of the counter. A coffee ring older than most of the tenants has fossilised on it.
furniture/furn_bld_897_1175_flyer_on_jac: A single-seat flyer up on jacks with its belly panels off and its guts hanging out, fuel lines capped, one wing spar bare to the metal. Somebody's been at it a long time, or gave up on it a long time ago; hard to say which. There's no tail number, and a clean rectangle where one used to be.
furniture/furn_mintcond_longboxes.json: White cardboard boxes as long as a forearm, lids off, on trestles down the length of the room. Card dividers stand up out of them in ranks, hand-lettered, and the hand got tidier over the years rather than worse. There's a system. It isn't the alphabet, and it has never been written down.
furniture/furn_bt_counter.json: A slab of end-grain maple on a steel frame, scrubbed pale and dished in the middle where forty years of the same cuts have worn it away. A spring scale hangs over it, its dial stopped near a number that's nobody's weight. Vesna Kroh works behind it, and doesn't put the cleaver down to talk to you.
furniture/furn_mintcond_dehumidifier.jso: A grey box on castors with a hose out of its belly into the floor drain, drawing the damp out of the building one bucket at a time. The gauge reads 41%, with a pencil mark beside it at 45 and another, angrier, at 50. It runs day and night. It's why the stock upstairs is worth anything.
furniture/furn_bt_walkin.json: An insulated steel door on a heavy latch, and behind it a room of stacked crates and hanging halves under a bulb in a wire cage. The cold comes out at you as a physical shove. There's a safety release on the inside, painted over, and a chalked tally that stopped being updated on a Thursday.
